Moniker

MON-ih-ker -- three syllables, stress on the first syllable, MON. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Moniker is a name or nickname that a person or thing is known by.

Fans gave the towering goalkeeper the moniker 'the Wall.'

Worked Example

The new late-night host introduces himself on air as Samuel R. Whitcombe III. The station manager winces and slides a note across the desk: 'Nobody remembers that. Pick a moniker.' By the next show, he is simply 'Sunrise Sam' -- and within a month, the whole town knows him.

'Sunrise Sam' is a moniker: a catchy name someone is known by, in place of (or alongside) the official one. Monikers stick because they are short, vivid, and easy to remember -- which is exactly why performers, athletes, and columnists so often work under one.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

nickname: an informal name used instead of the real one

alias: a false or alternate name used to hide identity

handle: an informal name, especially online or on the radio

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

given name: the official first name received at birth

legal name: the name on official documents

Where it sits · how much the name conceals — nickname → moniker → alias

nickname vs. moniker: Nickname is friendly and open -- everyone knows both the nickname and the real name behind it.

alias vs. moniker: Alias is the strongest and most secretive: a moniker or nickname is worn in public, but an alias exists to conceal who someone really is -- it is the word police reports reach for.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — munik

root — munik: name (possibly Shelta (the language of Irish Travellers), from Irish ainm 'name')

Put it together

Put it together: Moniker surfaced as street slang in the 1800s, and its paper trail runs out quickly: the best guess traces it to Shelta, the language of Irish Travellers, where munik meant 'name' -- itself scrambled from Irish ainm. Because the word was passed along by speech rather than in writing, its exact route is unsettled, which is why the origin is marked uncertain.

Use the root in a new word: namesake

Use the root in a new word: namesake: The baby is her grandmother's namesake, sharing her full name.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Moniker is an informal, slightly playful word -- the register of sportswriters and headlines: 'the rookie earned the moniker...' It covers everything from affectionate nicknames to stage names to a trucker's radio handle. It is neutral about honesty; when a name exists specifically to hide someone's identity, the sharper word is alias.
